docs.title: zoo-argowf-runner
docs.text: zoo-argowf-runner is a ZOO-Project runner that executes CWL Application Packages on Kubernetes using Argo Workflows.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The package provides ZooArgoWorkflowsRunner, which submits a CWL Application Package to an Argo Workflows WorkflowTemplate, monitors the resulting Workflow, and maps its outputs back to ZOO-Project. It builds on shared foundations from zoo-runner-common rather than reimplementing runner plumbing from scratch.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
zoo-runner-common: BaseRunner (abstract)
        │
        └── ZooArgoWorkflowsRunner (this package)
                │
                ▼
        Argo Workflows WorkflowTemplate ("calrissian-runner")
                │
                ▼
        Calrissian Job — runs the CWL Application Package on Kubernetes

ZooArgoWorkflowsRunner inherits most of its interface unchanged from BaseRunner — this package only adds what's specific to Argo Workflows: submitting the Workflow, monitoring it, and translating its outputs.

docs.title: ExecutionHandler API Reference
docs.text: zoo_argowf_runner.handlers re-exports this class from zoo-runner-common for convenience — from zoo_argowf_runner.handlers import ExecutionHandler works without an extra import line in service code. The class itself is abstract: subclasses must implement each hook shown above.

docs.title: ExecutionHandler
docs.text:
Bases: ABC

Abstract base class for execution handlers.

Execution handlers provide hooks that allow customization of CWL workflow execution behavior at various stages. Subclasses must implement all abstract methods to provide concrete execution logic.

docs.title: get_additional_parameters() abstractmethod
docs.text:
Get additional parameters for workflow execution.

Returns:

Name Type Description dict

Dictionary of parameter names to values

These parameters will be merged with the workflow inputs and can be used to provide configuration or runtime parameters.

docs.title: get_pod_env_vars() abstractmethod
docs.text:
Get environment variables for execution pods/containers.

Returns:

Name Type Description dict

Dictionary of environment variable names to values

These environment variables will be set in the execution environment (e.g., Kubernetes pods, Docker containers).

docs.title: get_pod_node_selector() abstractmethod
docs.text:
Get node selector for scheduling execution pods.

Returns:

Name Type Description dict

Dictionary of node selector labels

Used in Kubernetes environments to control which nodes can run the execution pods. Return empty dict for no node selection.

docs.title: get_secrets() abstractmethod
docs.text:
Get secrets required for workflow execution.

Returns:

Name Type Description dict

Dictionary of secret names to secret values

Use this to provide credentials, API keys, or other sensitive configuration data needed during execution.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: A minimal ZOO service built with ZooArgoWorkflowsRunner, adapted from the water_bodies example in the repository's tests/ folder.

docs.title: 1. Implement an ExecutionHandler
docs.text:
from loguru import logger
from zoo_argowf_runner.runner import ExecutionHandler, ZooArgoWorkflowsRunner


class ArgoWFRunnerExecutionHandler(ExecutionHandler):
    def __init__(self, conf):
        self.conf = conf

    def get_pod_env_vars(self):
        return {"A": "1", "B": "1"}

    def get_pod_node_selector(self):
        return None

    def get_secrets(self):
        pass

    def get_additional_parameters(self):
        return {
            "s3_bucket": "results",
            "sub_path": self.conf["lenv"]["usid"],
            "region_name": "it-rom",
            "endpoint_url": "http://minio.ns1.svc.cluster.local:9000",
        }

    def handle_outputs(self, log, output, usage_report, tool_logs, **kwargs):
        execution = kwargs.get("execution")
        tool_logs = execution.get_tool_logs()
        # map tool_logs into self.conf["service_logs"] for ZOO to expose

docs.title: 2. Wire it up in a ZOO service
docs.text:
service.py must implement {workflow_id}(conf, inputs, outputs):

import os, pathlib, yaml

try:
    import zoo
except ImportError:
    from zoo_runner_common.zoostub import ZooStub

    zoo = ZooStub()


def water_bodies(conf, inputs, outputs):
    with open(
        os.path.join(pathlib.Path(__file__).parent.absolute(), "app-package.cwl")
    ) as stream:
        cwl = yaml.safe_load(stream)

    runner = ZooArgoWorkflowsRunner(
        cwl=cwl,
        conf=conf,
        inputs=inputs,
        outputs=outputs,
        execution_handler=ArgoWFRunnerExecutionHandler(conf=conf),
    )
    exit_status = runner.execute()

    if exit_status == zoo.SERVICE_SUCCEEDED:
        outputs = runner.outputs
        return zoo.SERVICE_SUCCEEDED

    conf["lenv"]["message"] = zoo._("Execution failed")
    return zoo.SERVICE_FAILED

docs.title: What runner.execute() does
docs.text:
1. Validates parameters and calls handler.pre_execution_hook().
  2. Merges handler.get_additional_parameters() with the CWL processing parameters.
  3. Submits the workflow, monitors it, and reports progress back to ZOO.
  4. Retrieves outputs, logs, and artifacts, then calls handler.handle_outputs().

See the Runner Guide for the env vars this depends on (ARGO_WF_ENDPOINT, etc.) and the full example in the repository.

docs.title: Handlers Guide
docs.text: zoo_argowf_runner.handlers.ExecutionHandler re-exports ExecutionHandler from zoo-runner-common. It's the customization point for ZooArgoWorkflowsRunner — the runner calls into it at each stage of execution, so service-specific logic (credentials, output handling) doesn't need to touch the runner itself.

docs.title: Methods to implement
docs.text: Method Called when Typical use pre_execution_hook() Before submission Validate environment get_additional_parameters() Building processing parameters Service-specific values (bucket, region, credentials) get_pod_env_vars() Building the pod spec Env vars for the Calrissian pod get_pod_node_selector() Building the pod spec Constrain scheduling get_secrets() Building the pod spec Attach Kubernetes secrets handle_outputs(log, output, usage_report, tool_logs, **kwargs) After execution Map outputs into conf/outputs post_execution_hook(...) After handle_outputs Cleanup, notifications

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from zoo_argowf_runner.handlers import ExecutionHandler


class MyExecutionHandler(ExecutionHandler):
    def __init__(self, conf):
        self.conf = conf

    def get_pod_env_vars(self):
        return {"MY_ENV_VAR": "value"}

    def get_pod_node_selector(self):
        return None

    def get_secrets(self):
        return None

    def get_additional_parameters(self):
        return {"s3_bucket": "results", "sub_path": self.conf["lenv"]["usid"]}

    def handle_outputs(self, log, output, usage_report, tool_logs, **kwargs):
        # process outputs here
        pass

Pass it in when constructing the runner:

runner = ZooArgoWorkflowsRunner(
    cwl=cwl,
    conf=conf,
    inputs=inputs,
    outputs=outputs,
    execution_handler=MyExecutionHandler(conf=conf),
)

docs.title: Runner Guide
docs.text: ZooArgoWorkflowsRunner inherits from BaseRunner in zoo-runner-common and adds the Argo-specific execute() implementation.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Description Default STORAGE_CLASS Kubernetes RWX storage class. standard DEFAULT_VOLUME_SIZE Calrissian default RWX volume size. 12Gi DEFAULT_MAX_CORES Calrissian default max cores. 4 DEFAULT_MAX_RAM Calrissian default max RAM. 4Gi ARGO_WF_ENDPOINT Argo Workflows API endpoint. http://localhost:2746 ARGO_WF_TOKEN Argo Workflows API token — see below. — ARGO_WF_SYNCHRONIZATION_CM Synchronization ConfigMap (key workflow). — ARGO_CWL_RUNNER_TEMPLATE WorkflowTemplate that runs the CWL. argo-cwl-runner ARGO_CWL_RUNNER_ENTRYPOINT Entrypoint template within it. calrissian-runner

Retrieve ARGO_WF_TOKEN with:

kubectl get -n ns1 secret argo.service-account-token -o=jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 --decode

docs.title: The Argo WorkflowTemplate interface
docs.text:
Argo Workflows must expose a WorkflowTemplate (or ClusterWorkflowTemplate) with this interface:

Inputs: parameters (JSON), cwl (JSON), max_ram, max_cores, entry_point.

Outputs: results (stdout), log (stderr), usage-report, stac-catalog, feature-collection.

Artifacts: tool-logs, calrissian-output, calrissian-stderr, calrissian-report.

See the example folder in the repository for a complete WorkflowTemplate implementing this interface.

docs.title: Caveat: additional volumes
docs.text:
If the WorkflowTemplate declares a volume (e.g. a ConfigMap for cwl-wrapper config), that volume must also be declared on the calling Workflow — Argo doesn't propagate volume declarations back to the caller. Use zoo_argowf_runner.volume.VolumeTemplates:

from zoo_argowf_runner.volume import VolumeTemplates

VolumeTemplates.create_config_map_volume(
    name="cwl-wrapper-config-vol",
    config_map_name="cwl-wrapper-config",
    items=[{"key": "main.yaml", "path": "main.yaml", "mode": 420}],
    default_mode=420,
    optional=False,
)

Keep the items keys in sync between the WorkflowTemplate and the caller — a mismatch is a common cause of "volume not found" errors at runtime.
